title: Protocol for synthesis and use of a turn-on fluorescent probe for quantifying labile Zn2+ in the Golgi apparatus in live cells
protocol: Weigh 0.780 g of 1,2,3,4-tetrahydroquinolin-7-ol.
Weigh 0.550 g of NaHCO3.
Weigh 82.0 mg of tetramethylammonium bromide.
Add 5.0 mL of H2O to a 50 mL two-neck round-bottom flask with a magnetic stirring bar.
Slowly add 1.43 g of tert-butyl 4-bromobutyrate at 0°C to the mixture in the flask.
Stir the suspension at room temperature for 70 hours.
Extract the reaction mixture with EtOAc using a separatory funnel (3 x 40 mL).
Wash the organic layer with brine (2 x 40 mL).
Dry the organic layer with MgSO4 and filter to remove the MgSO4.
Remove volatile material using a rotary evaporator under reduced pressure to obtain a brown oil.
Purify the crude product using silica gel column chromatography (EtOAc/hexane = 8/92).
Afford compound 2 as a pale yellow oil.
Use a syringe to add 2.0 mL of dry DMF in a 50 mL dried two-neck round-bottom flask under N2.
Add POCl3 dropwise to the flask containing dry DMF at 0°C.
Stir the solution for 5 min at 0°C.
Stir the mixture for 15 min at room temperature (20–25°C).
Cool down the mixture to 0°C and add compound 2 in 2.0 mL of dry DMF dropwise using a syringe.
Stir the reaction mixture at 0°C for 5 min.
After stirring at room temperature for 24 h, pour the reaction mixture into 25 mL of cold saturated aqueous solution of NaHCO3.
Extract the mixture using EtOAc/Et2O (1:1) in a separatory funnel.
Dry the organic layers with Na2SO4.
Condense the organic layers using a rotary evaporator to afford compound 3 as pale yellow oil.
Weigh 1.91 g of compound 3.
Add 0.740 mL of ethyl nitroacetate.
Add 90 μL of piperidine.
Add 180 μL of AcOH.
Add 60 mL of 1-butanol to a dried two-neck round-bottom flask under N2.
Stir the suspension for 5 hours at 120°C.
Cool the mixture to 0°C.
Collect the resulting precipitate by filtration.
Wash the precipitate with 20 mL of 1-butanol.
Wash the precipitate with 20 mL of hexane.
Dry the solid in vacuo at 50°C to obtain compound 4 as a red solid.
Weigh 301 mg of compound 4.
Add 20 mL of MeOH/CH2Cl2 (3:1, v/v) to a round-bottom flask with a magnetic stirring bar.
Add 9.8 mg of Pd/C.
Place an H2 balloon with a three-way stopcock on the flask.
Replace the atmosphere with H2 using three vacuum–fill cycles.
Stir at room temperature (20–25°C) for 3 h under H2.
Filter the reaction mixture via celite.
Wash the celite with MeOH and CH2Cl2.
Remove the volatile material using a rotary evaporator under reduced pressure to afford a crude product.
Purify the crude product using silica gel column chromatography (EtOAc/hexane = 15/85).
Afford compound 5 as pale yellow oil.
Characterize the product by 1H and 13C NMR spectroscopies and ESI-MS.
Store the product at 4°C for at least 3 months.
Stir the mixture at 90°C for 25 hours under N2.
Cool the reaction mixture to room temperature (20-25°C).
Extract the reaction mixture with CH2Cl2.
Wash the organic layer with water twice, each time using 50 mL.
Wash the organic layer with a 2% aqueous solution of Na2S2O3 twice, each time using 50 mL.
Wash the organic layer with brine twice, each time using 50 mL.
Dry the organic layer with Na2SO4.
Remove the solvents using a rotary evaporator.
Purify the crude product using amino-functionalized silica gel column chromatography (MeOH/CH2Cl2 = 5/95).
Afford compound 6 as a brown oil and store at 4°C for up to 3 months.
Weigh 101 mg of compound 6 and add it in a dried two-neck round-bottom flask under N2.
Add 4.0 mL of dry CH2Cl2 and 0.50 mL of TFA using syringes.
Stir the mixture at room temperature (20-25°C) for 13 hours.
Remove volatile materials using a rotary evaporator to afford ZnDA-1 as a brown oil.
Use the crude product in the next step without further purification.
Add 92.0 mg of crude ZnDA-1 in a 100 mL dried two-neck flask under N2.
Add 4.0 mL of dry DMF using a syringe.
Add 50.1 mg of EDC·HCl, 60.8 mg of 2-(2-((6-chlorohexyl)oxy)ethoxy)ethan-1-amine, and 45.0 mg of HOBt·H2O.
Add dry Et3N (75.0 μL).
Stir at room temperature for 78 h under N2.
Add 20 mL of water to the mixture.
Extract the mixture with CH2Cl2.
Wash the organic layer with saturated aqueous solution of NaHCO3 (2 × 20 mL).
Wash the organic layer with water (2 × 20 mL).
Wash the organic layer with 10% citric acid (2 × 20 mL).
Wash the organic layer with brine (2 × 20 mL).
Dry the organic layer with Na2SO4.
Remove the solvent using a rotary evaporator.
Purify the mixture using amino-functionalized silica gel column chromatography (EtOAc/hexane = 30/70) to afford ZnDA-1H as a mixture.
Further purify using reversed-phase HPLC (0.1% HCOOH in water/MeCN = 80/20 (v/v, 0 min), 20/80 (v/v, 15 min), 0/100 (v/v, 20 min), and 0/100 (v/v, 30 min)).
Lyophilize the fractions to afford ZnDA-1H as a yellow oil.
Characterize the product by 1H NMR spectroscopy.
Characterize the product by 13C NMR spectroscopy.
Characterize the product by ESI-MS.
Pause point: Store the product at 4°C for at least 3 months.
Monitor reaction progress using TLC.
Detach HeLa cells from a 60-mm culture dish.
Wash detached cells twice with Ca2+/Mg2+-free PBS.
Add 500 μL of PBS and 500 μL of trypsin/EDTA solution to the dish.
Incubate cells at 37°C for 2 minutes.
Add 500 μL of antibiotics-free MEM containing 10% FBS.
Suspend detached cells using gentle pipetting.
Take 10 μL of cell suspension and mix with 10 μL of trypan blue stain.
Add the mixture to a hemocytometer.
Count the cell number under a microscope.
Seed HeLa cells in a 35-mm glass-bottom dish.
Add 2 mL of antibiotics-free MEM containing 10% FBS to the dish.
Add 2.5 × 10^4 cells to the dish.
Gently shake the dish with an upwards and downwards motion.
Incubate seeded cells for 24 hours at 37°C in a humidified incubator with 5% CO2.
Adjust the number of cells to be seeded according to the cell proliferation rate.
Transfect cells with a HaloTag expression vector using FuGENE HD as the transfection reagent.
Add 100 μL of Opti-MEM to a sterile 1.5 mL tube.
Add 150 ng of plasmid DNA (pEF4MycHisB-hManII-Halo) and mix by pipetting.
Add 1.05 μL of FuGENE HD and mix immediately by pipetting.
Incubate the mixture for 15 min at room temperature (20–25°C).
Add the transfection mixture to the imaging dish.
Gently shake the dish with an upwards and downwards motion and from left to right.
Incubate the cells for 36 h at 37°C in a humidified incubator containing 5% CO2.
Avoid using antibiotics during transfection.
Optimize the total amount of plasmid DNA for transfection.
Optimize the ratio of FuGENE HD to DNA for transfection.
Optimize the incubation time after adding the transfection reagent/DNA mixture.
Use 150 ng of plasmid DNA to avoid high cell death and mislocalization.
Set up the microscope by turning on the temperature controller and light source.
Choose an appropriate objective lens.
Assemble the hand-made solution injection tool.
Insert the stainless tube into an inlet port.
Place the tip of the injection tool close to the top of the glass part of the dish.
Clean and moisten the interior of the injection tube using 70% EtOH (2 × 200 μL).
Aspirate the medium from the imaging dish.
Wash twice with 1 mL of HBSS (+).
Add 990 μL of DMEM containing 4 mM glutamine to the dish.
Add 10 μL of DMEM containing 4 mM glutamine, 25 μM ZnDA-1H, and 0.50 μM HTL-TMR.
Gently shake the dish after adding the solution.
Incubate the dish for 30 min at 37°C in a humidified incubator with 5% CO2.
Wash twice with 1 mL of HBSS (+).
Add 1.9 mL of chelexed HHBSS buffer supplemented with Ca²⁺ and Zn²⁺ to the dish.
Supplement 180 μL of chelexed HHBSS buffer with 18.2 μL of 20 mM ZnSO₄.
Heat the solution along with 200 μM TPEN solution at 37°C.
Add a drop of proper oil to the objective lens if necessary.
Place the dish on a pre-warmed on-stage incubation chamber of an inverted laser scanning confocal microscope.
Replace the normal dish lid with a lid that has a small hole.
Insert the end of the injection tube into the hole in the new lid.
Set imaging parameters in FluoView software.
Select excitation lasers at 473 nm and 559 nm for ZnDA-1H and HTL-TMR, respectively.
Choose emission filters at 490–540 nm for ZnDA-1H and 575–675 nm for HTL-TMR.
Select the high-sensitivity GaAsP detector as light path.
Set dichroic mirror at 560 nm.
Adjust scan speed to 2.0 μs/pixel, frame size to 1024 × 1024 pixels, and zoom to 1.0.
Configure laser power at 0.2% for both excitation lasers.
Select a 60× silicone oil-immersion objective lens (NA 1.30).
Enable ZDC AF during Time Series Scan in the autofocus settings.
Set time interval to 30 s with scan number set to 27.
Adjust HV between 500 and 700 for sufficient fluorescence signals, gain at 1, offset at 0, and confocal aperture at 120 (auto).
Find and focus cells showing fluorescence signals of both probes with proper protein localization.
Mix 2.2 μL of 2.0 mM pyrithione in DMSO with chelexed HHBSS buffer supplemented with Zn2+.
Start image acquisition.
Add 100 μL of 200 μM TPEN solution (final concentration 10 μM) after 2 min to obtain minimum intensity values of ZnDA-1H.
Mix 200 μL of ZPT solution (final concentration 400 μM Zn²⁺/2.0 μM pyrithione).
Wash the injection tube interior with 70% EtOH and water (2 × 200 μL).
Wipe off the oil from the objective lens.
Incubate the imaging dish for 15 min in the on-stage incubation chamber before image acquisition.
Position the end of the injection tube over the glass part of the dish, not touching the imaging medium.
Use 0.2% laser power (Head output: 473 nm: 15 mW; 559 nm: 15 mW) to avoid photobleaching of the probes.
Adjust HV and gain values so that ZnDA-1H fluorescence signals are not saturated upon addition of ZPT.
Do not add TPEN and ZPT solutions during scanning.
Open time-lapse images using FIJI software.
Apply a median filter to both ZnDA-1H and HTL-TMR channels with 1.0 pixel size.
Measure the mean intensity in the cell-free region as background.
Subtract the measured mean value from each image.
Select the target organelle within single cells using the TMR channel mask created by the Otsu threshold algorithm.
Create a mask image from the TMR channel and apply it to both TMR and ZnDA channels to isolate fluorescence intensity from the target organelle.
Duplicate the HTL-TMR channel stack: Image -> Duplicate (shortcut: ctrl + shift + [d]).
Threshold the ROIs of the duplicated HTL-TMR channel stack: Image -> Adjust -> Threshold (shortcut: ctrl + shift + [t]).
Choose a proper algorithm to extract the desired ROIs.
Convert the thresholded ROIs into binary: Process -> Math -> Divide -> Enter “255” -> Press “OK”.
Press “Yes” when asked if you want to “Process all images”.
Save the binary stack as “mask.tiff”.
Apply the mask to both ZnDA-1H and HTL-TMR channel stacks: Process -> Image Calculator.

Select the file for the ZnDA-1H channel stack as Image 1 and the mask file as Image 2, select “Multiply” in the operation tab, and put checks to “Create new window” and “32-bit (float) result”. Press “OK”.
Press “Yes” when asked if you want to “Process all images”.
Repeat for the HTL-TMR channel stack.
Draw a circle to select the ROI for each cell in the HTL-TMR channel stack and add it to the ROI manager (shortcut: [t]).
Set measurements to obtain the total fluorescence intensity in the ROIs: Analyze -> Set Measurements -> Put a check to “Integrated density”.
Select ROIs in the ROI manager for ZnDA-1H channel stack.
Choose "More -> Multi Measure" to measure fluorescence intensity.
Check “Measure all slices” and “One row per slice” options.
Press “OK” to start measurement.
Save the results as a CSV file.
Repeat steps for HTL-TMR channel stack.
Open the CSV files containing fluorescence data.
Calculate the ratio of ZnDA-1H/HTL-TMR.
Plot the calculated ratios using Microsoft Excel or KaleidaGraph.
Calculate labile Zn2+ concentration in the Golgi apparatus using the equation [Zn2+]Golgi = Kd × (Rss – Rmin)/(Rmax – Rss).
Use a Kd value of 0.54 ± 0.05 μM for the calculation.
Alternatively, estimate [Zn2+]Golgi at different pH conditions by applying corresponding Kd values.
